text: A window is a tree of components. What survives when you move from Swing to a browser?
choices: Only the event loop, since HTML has no component hierarchy.
Nothing structural; a web interface is built on fundamentally different concepts.
The tree, the layout principle, the event loop, and the model/view separation — everything except the widget API.
Only the model/view separation; the browser's rendering model shares nothing else.
explanation: HTML's DOM is that tree, CSS flexbox is that layout principle, JavaScript's single-threaded event loop is that loop with the same rule about not blocking it, and every front-end framework is arguing about that separation. Which is why the chapter is not a Swing tutorial: the toolkit is documentation and the shape is the transferable part.
